questions.text: Mobile Money Provider Financial Sustainability - SSA: Demonstrate long-term financial viability: (1) Revenue model (transaction fees, interest, data monetization - sustainable?); (2) Profitability (is mobile money business profitable? timeline?); (3) Funding sources (parent company, investors, revenue - diversified?); (4) Burn rate vs runway (how long can operate?); (5) Local entity financials (not just parent - local operations viable?); (6) Currency risk management (local currency volatility - hedging?); (7) User affordability (fees sustainable for low-income users?).
questions.evidence_required: Financial statements (local entity), Revenue model documentation, Profitability data, Funding sources, Burn rate analysis, Currency hedging, Affordability analysis
questions.africa_specific_notes: Mobile money profitability challenging (low-value transactions, high costs). Currency volatility major risk. Local entity must be viable. User affordability critical (can't price out poor).

questions.text: Customer Fund Safety & Protection: Ensure user funds are protected: (1) Customer fund segregation (user funds separate from company funds?); (2) Trust account management (funds held in trust at licensed bank?); (3) Deposit insurance (are user funds insured? up to what amount?); (4) Bankruptcy protection (what happens to user funds if provider fails?); (5) Regulatory safeguards (central bank requirements for fund protection); (6) Audit trail (can user funds be accounted for?); (7) Fund repatriation (can users withdraw all funds anytime?).
questions.evidence_required: Fund segregation documentation, Trust account details, Insurance certificates, Bankruptcy procedures, Regulatory compliance, Audit reports, Withdrawal policies
questions.africa_specific_notes: Customer fund safety = most critical. Mobile money provider failures have occurred. Segregation mandatory (central bank requirement). Insurance limited. Users must be able to withdraw anytime.

questions.text: Exit Risk & User Fund Protection: Plan for provider failure or exit: (1) What happens to user funds if provider shuts down (full refund? timeline?); (2) What happens to user transaction history (data portability?); (3) What happens to user credit history (can users take to other lenders?); (4) Transition plan (how are users migrated to alternative providers?); (5) Regulatory oversight of exit (central bank supervises?); (6) Communication plan (how are users notified?); (7) Historical exit cases (have other providers exited? how handled?).
questions.evidence_required: Exit plan documentation, Fund refund procedures, Data portability, Credit history transfer, Transition plan, Regulatory oversight, Historical exit analysis
questions.africa_specific_notes: Provider exit risk real (some have failed). Users' life savings at risk. Exit planning mandatory. Central bank must supervise. Historical cases: some users lost funds (unacceptable).

questions.text: Long-Term Mobile Money Market Commitment - SSA: Demonstrate sustained commitment: (1) Years of operation in Sub-Saharan Africa (not just pilots - sustained operations); (2) Geographic expansion (growing presence or retreating?); (3) User base growth (acquiring new users or losing existing?); (4) Product roadmap (continued investment in features?); (5) Multi-year regulatory commitments (license renewals, compliance investments); (6) Agent network expansion (investing in distribution?); (7) Financial inclusion commitment (serving unbanked or just profitable segments?).
questions.evidence_required: Operational history (3+ years), Geographic expansion data, User growth metrics, Product roadmap, Regulatory commitments, Agent network growth, Financial inclusion metrics
questions.africa_specific_notes: Long-term commitment critical (users' life savings). Some providers have exited. Geographic expansion = commitment signal. User growth important. Financial inclusion vs profit tension.

questions.text: Mobile Money Track Record & Reliability: Demonstrate proven track record: (1) Operational history (how many years? how many countries?); (2) User base (how many active users? transaction volume?); (3) System reliability history (uptime track record); (4) Fraud management track record (how well prevented/resolved?); (5) Regulatory compliance history (any violations? penalties?); (6) User satisfaction (NPS, retention rates); (7) Industry recognition (awards, certifications).
questions.evidence_required: Operational history documentation, User base metrics, Uptime history, Fraud management data, Regulatory compliance record, User satisfaction metrics, Industry recognition
questions.africa_specific_notes: Track record critical for trust. Operational history important (new entrants risky). User base size = network effects. Reliability history key. Regulatory violations = red flag.

questions.text: User Financial Inclusion Outcomes - SSA: Provide rigorous evidence of financial inclusion impact: (1) Financial access (% of unbanked now accessing formal financial services); (2) Savings behavior (are users saving more?); (3) Credit access (can users access credit?); (4) Resilience (can users cope with shocks better?); (5) Economic empowerment (income, business growth); (6) Gender impact (are women benefiting equally?); (7) Study quality (RCTs, quasi-experimental, or just testimonials?).
questions.evidence_required: Financial inclusion studies (RCTs preferred), Savings data, Credit access data, Resilience indicators, Economic impact data, Gender-disaggregated outcomes, Study methodology
questions.africa_specific_notes: Financial inclusion impact critical (not just adoption). Savings behavior important. Credit access key benefit. Gender impact essential (women often excluded). RCTs preferred (rigorous evidence).

questions.text: User References & Testimonials - Mobile Money: Provide verifiable user references: (1) User testimonials (video, audio, written - in local languages); (2) User contact information (can prospective users talk to existing users?); (3) Agent testimonials (do agents recommend service?); (4) Geographic diversity (references from multiple regions, countries); (5) User demographics (references from women, youth, elderly, different income levels); (6) Negative feedback transparency (are complaints/criticisms shared?); (7) Independent user surveys (third-party satisfaction data).
questions.evidence_required: User testimonial library (video, audio, local languages), Referenceable user list, Agent testimonials, Geographic diversity, Demographic diversity, Complaint transparency, Independent surveys
questions.africa_specific_notes: Testimonials must be authentic (not paid actors). User-to-user trust critical. Agent testimonials powerful. Must include negative feedback (credibility). Independent surveys important.

questions.text: Third-Party Validation & Recognition - Mobile Money: Demonstrate external validation: (1) Central bank endorsement (regulatory approval, positive statements); (2) Development partner support (World Bank, USAID, Gates Foundation); (3) Industry awards (GSMA Mobile Money awards, fintech competitions); (4) Research institution partnerships (universities, think tanks validating impact); (5) Media coverage (credible journalism, not just press releases); (6) Peer recognition (other mobile money providers, industry associations); (7) International standards compliance (GSMA Mobile Money API, ISO).
questions.evidence_required: Central bank approvals, Development partner grants/contracts, Award certifications, Research partnerships, Media coverage, Industry recognition, Standards compliance
questions.africa_specific_notes: Central bank endorsement critical. Development partner support important (credibility). Awards less important than outcomes. Research partnerships valuable. Standards compliance emerging.

questions.text: Fee Fairness & Anti-Exploitation - Mobile Money: Demonstrate fair, non-exploitative pricing: (1) Fee transparency (all fees disclosed, no hidden charges); (2) Fee competitiveness (vs other providers, banks); (3) Fee affordability (reasonable for low-income users?); (4) Interest rate fairness (for credit - APR vs informal lenders, not predatory); (5) Pricing audits (independent verification of fairness); (6) User pricing feedback (do users feel pricing is fair?); (7) Vulnerable user protection (special pricing for elderly, disabled?).
questions.evidence_required: Fee disclosure documentation, Competitive pricing analysis, Affordability analysis, Interest rate comparisons, Independent pricing audits, User pricing surveys, Vulnerable user policies
questions.africa_specific_notes: Fee fairness critical (users very price-sensitive). Hidden fees destroy trust. Interest rates must not be predatory. Vulnerable users need protection. Pricing audits important.

questions.text: Data Ethics & User Data Sovereignty - Mobile Money: Ensure ethical data practices: (1) User data ownership (users own their data, not platform); (2) Data usage consent (informed, specific, voluntary); (3) Data benefit sharing (if data monetized, do users benefit?); (4) Data sovereignty (user data stays in Africa, not extracted?); (5) Credit scoring ethics (no discrimination, bias testing); (6) Research ethics (if data used for research, users consented? IRB approval?); (7) Data colonialism prevention (value from data shared with users).
questions.evidence_required: Data ownership policies, Consent mechanisms, Data benefit sharing, Data residency policies, Credit scoring bias testing, Research ethics approvals, Anti-data colonialism policies
questions.africa_specific_notes: Data ethics critical (transaction data reveals everything). Data colonialism concern (value extracted). Users must own and benefit from data. Credit scoring bias risk (gender, geography).

questions.text: Social Impact & Financial Inclusion Commitment: Demonstrate positive social impact: (1) Financial inclusion metrics (% unbanked served); (2) Women's financial inclusion (gender-disaggregated data); (3) Rural financial inclusion (urban vs rural access); (4) Youth financial inclusion (young people served); (5) Agent employment (how many jobs created? quality?); (6) Local economic impact (transaction volume, economic activity); (7) Financial literacy investment (supporting education).
questions.evidence_required: Financial inclusion metrics, Gender-disaggregated data, Rural access data, Youth inclusion data, Agent employment data, Economic impact studies, Financial literacy programs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Financial inclusion = core mission (not just profit). Women's inclusion critical. Rural access essential. Youth important (future users). Agent jobs significant. Economic impact measurable.

questions.text: Ethical Debt Collection Practices: Ensure respectful and legal debt recovery: (1) Harassment prevention (no excessive calling, no threats); (2) Privacy respect (no contacting friends/family/employers without consent); (3) Data privacy in collection (no public shaming lists); (4) Agent conduct (training for collection agents); (5) Hardship policies (options for users in genuine distress); (6) Regulatory compliance (adherence to consumer protection laws on debt collection).
questions.evidence_required: Debt collection policy, Agent training logs, Complaint records regarding harassment
questions.africa_specific_notes: Digital lenders in SSA often use shaming tactics. Ethical collection is a major trust differentiator.

scoring_notes: Layer 5 (Integrity) for Financial Services in Sub-Saharan Africa: Customer fund safety is paramount - segregation and insurance mandatory. Provider financial sustainability critical (users' life savings at risk). Fee fairness essential (no exploitation). Data ethics and user data sovereignty non-negotiable. Financial inclusion outcomes must be measurable.
